projectDescription: A new general-purpose 3D creation environment where AI agents create, inspect, modify, validate and revise scenes through a typed modeling API, and humans direct and directly edit everything.

context.userWorkflow: Stated 2026-11-03 at Decision 9: user drives modeling from VS Code / Claude Code; the website is a live view (watch, inspect, review), not the primary input surface.

decisions.title: Where the app runs

options.A: Headless core + browser first (Electron later)

decisions.caseAgainst: General-purpose production work is desktop-class (multi-GB scenes, native FBX/USD SDKs, real folders); browser limits (4GB WASM, Chromium-only folder access) may bake in; if an installer is needed within ~3 months, Electron from day one avoids a migration.
assumptions: Prototype ~6 weeks, scenes well under 4GB
Chromium acceptable for real file workflow
Engine package enforced DOM-free from commit one
tripwires: Need native SDKs (FBX, USD C++) or scenes approach 2-3GB -> wrap in Electron

decisions.title: Scene source of truth & change model

options.A: Simple store + undo stack
options.B: Records + branching change log (patch transactions, content-addressed mesh blobs)

decisions.caseAgainst: Building a mini version-control system before proposals are proven; event-sourcing replay/migration tax; Loro gives fork/checkout/merge for free; Option A suffices for weeks 1-2.
assumptions: Edits flow through one validated typed-tool pipeline
Proposals/variants are a core differentiator
Meshes stored by content hash; snapshots every N commits
tripwires: Need simultaneous same-object multi-agent edits with auto-merge -> put Loro under the same record API

decisions.title: Construction model

options.A: Modifier stack
options.D: Typed op graph + code view (named params, named anchors)

decisions.caseAgainst: Designing a language + editor is where solo projects die; benchmark geometric correctness ~0.35 regardless of format; much general-purpose content (characters, sculpts) isn't parametric, so a modifier stack might ship faster.
assumptions: Start with 15-25 ops, grow from benchmark failures
editableMesh escape-hatch op
Named anchors/datums, never face indices
Node view can be layered later
tripwires: If >40% of benchmark objects need raw mesh escapes, add a modifier-stack layer for mesh objects

decisions.title: Geometry kernel strategy

options.A: Manifold only
options.C: Kernel interface: Manifold + TS half-edge EditMesh + OpenSubdiv, OCCT lazy later

decisions.caseAgainst: Three kernels = three failure modes and buggy seams; mesh->B-rep is not recoverable; hand-written half-edge is subtle; Manifold-only for months proves the AI loop first.
assumptions: Weeks 1-3 Manifold only behind the interface
Explicit conversion ops with validity checks
All kernels in a Worker (browser) / in-process (Node)
tripwires: Manifold boolean artifacts in >5% of benchmark runs -> mesh-repair pass or OCCT booleans for those ops

decisions.title: How AI models talk to the app
decisions.chosenTitle: Claude Code skill (/studio) -> studio CLI generated from the zod registry -> engine daemon; browser is a live view; MCP adapter optional later
decisions.reasoning: User wants to interact via a Claude Code skill, like /x-decide; the website is just the view.

history.change: User workflow note: drive from VS Code / Claude Code; website is just the view -> MCP primary, in-app agent deferred.
Changed to custom: interact via a Claude Code skill. Registry now emits a CLI (primary) + optional MCP adapter; in-app agent dropped; run_script becomes `studio run file.ts`.

downstreamImpacts: D6: renders produced by the view on request from the daemon; CLI returns image paths Claude Code reads
D8: right panel = Claude Code activity feed + review instead of chat
D9: Keep/Undo in the view and via `studio keep/undo/commit`
D10: first slice = /studio makes a stool that appears in the view

options.A: MCP server only
options.C: One zod tool registry exposed as MCP + in-app agent (AI SDK 6), run_script code mode later

decisions.caseAgainst: Two surfaces to maintain; MCP door serves developers not novices; code-mode evidence (Anthropic, Cloudflare, CodeAct) suggests starting with code could be more efficient.
assumptions: Tools grouped in modes, <=~20 visible, tool search beyond
Structured results + actionable validation errors
run_script only in QuickJS-WASM, produces commits only
MCP door initially for dev/benchmarks
tripwires: >15 tool calls per benchmark task or token budget exceeded -> promote run_script to default

decisions.title: AI perception loop

options.A: Structured diagnostics only
options.C: Deterministic checks (authority) + labeled separate views at milestones

decisions.caseAgainst: Visual feedback gains are modest (~18% in CADCodeVerify; ground-truth solver beat it); images cost 5-10x tokens; headless rendering is fiddly; Option A alone is a leaner start.
assumptions: Checks every commit; images at milestones or on demand
Persistent render page, never fresh browser per frame
Rules attach to semantic types, grow from benchmark failures
Critic added later, different model family, gated on checks
tripwires: Visual checks change outcome in <10% of benchmark runs after 2 weeks -> images on-demand only

decisions.title: Visual direction of the workspace

options.A: Soft Premium (Instrument Sans, stone + sage)
options.C: Kinetic Modern dark (Space Grotesk + Manrope, navy + lime)
options.D: Editorial Print (Fraunces + Source Serif 4, paper + brick)

decisions.tiebreaker: First 50 users are AI devs via Claude Code -> B; designers who never learned Blender -> A
decisions.caseAgainst: 3D tools default dark for glare/long sessions; early adopters likely technical (fits B).
assumptions: North-star user is the creative director
Neutral viewport surround
Dark variant ships later via tokens
Technical depth one click away
tripwires: Repeated dark-mode requests or 'too soft for real work' -> ship dark variant first
decisions.fontNote: Library body face Inter replaced with deliberate per-tradition faces

decisions.title: Workspace layout
decisions.note: User chose A over a LEAN recommendation of B; design effort shifts to Decision 9 (review UX).

options.A: Docked panels
options.B: Viewport stage (floating contextual cards, AI command bar, history scrubber, dock toggle)

decisions.tiebreaker: If exploring many variants is the core loop, Variant Canvas (C) — or as the Proposals tab inside B
decisions.caseAgainst: Floating contextual UI is harder to build well; docked panels ship in days and free effort for review UX.
assumptions: Dock-panels toggle from day one
Floating cards avoid selection bounds
Variant canvas as secondary Proposals mode
Review style settled in Decision 9
tripwires: Testers spend more time moving cards than modeling -> default to docked

decisions.title: How AI changes are reviewed
decisions.workflowNote: Review UI lives in the web view's right panel; Claude Code can also keep/undo via MCP tools (keep_change, undo_change, commit_proposal).

options.A: Ghost overlay
options.D: Change-by-change review (semantic change list, per-change Keep/Undo, viewport highlight, before/after flip)

decisions.caseAgainst: Turns a visual craft into reading a diff; dependent changes need rules and re-checks; granularity is overhead if most proposals are cohesive.
assumptions: AI groups changes into named meaningful steps
B's cards as tabs for multiple alternatives
Dependent changes linked; checks re-run after partial keep
Nothing deleted — archived branches
tripwires: Whole-proposal accept/discard >90% of the time -> collapse list behind details toggle

decisions.title: First build sequence
decisions.reasoning: User: 'Just build it all out' — recommendation applied.

options.A: Six horizontal layers
options.B: Thin vertical slice (stool via /studio by end of week 2), then thicken

decisions.caseAgainst: Slices tempt corner-cutting in one-way-door foundations; 'thicken later' often means never. Mitigation: real Scene IR/commit format and anchors from day one.
assumptions: Week 1 uses real Scene IR + commit format
Stool benchmark is slice acceptance test; harness week 3
Prototype estimates, ~full-time with Claude Code
Week-2 view = bare Three.js page over websocket
tripwires: Stool not appearing end-to-end by day 12 -> stop features, cut scope

decisions.title: Shape of the game toolset

options.A: One studio grows into a game maker (own browser runtime)
options.B: Family of studios on a shared core + own web runtime
options.C: Asset forge (this studio) + a real engine via a /game bridge skill

decisions.caseAgainst: Splits the world at the asset hand-off where pipelines break (materials on reimport, skinned animation), and engine-side edits lose the studio's branching review.
assumptions: Goal is making games, not selling an engine
Studio's edge is checked, reviewable asset making
Target engine drivable headless from CLI
Hand-off owned by a checked export contract with round-trip tests
tripwires: Round-trip export tests fail repeatedly for skinned characters -> reconsider B for characters
You find yourself wanting to sell the engine -> revisit D

decisions.title: Target art style

options.A: Low-poly, palette + material presets (PBR values travel in glTF)
options.E: Low-poly + procedural materials auto-baked to textures on export (auto-UV)

decisions.caseAgainst: Crowded look; and with A alone the studio’s procedural grain/glaze won’t show in-game until the bake (E) exists. Pick E now if the game must match the studio from day one.
assumptions: Solo/tiny team, Claude does most asset work
Palette + one shading model gives a recognizable look
Game-pipeline default, not a limit on the studio's prop materials
tripwires: Playtesters call the look generic -> add toon/outline shader and art-direct palette before considering B
Characters feel lifeless -> revisit for characters only

history.change: User asked whether in-progress materials work was considered; added material presets to A, added option E (baked procedural materials), recommendation A→E path, confidence strong→lean.

decisions.reasoning: User picked E (game should match the studio’s materials) over the lean recommendation A→E path.

decisions.title: Game targets: Godot for games, three.js for the web
decisions.chosenTitle: Two targets (Godot + three.js), one asset contract

options.A: Two targets (Godot standalone, three.js web), one shared asset contract; /game with two back ends
options.D: Two targets + a portable game/level format compiled to each

decisions.caseAgainst: Doubles what Claude must master (two languages, physics, run/screenshot paths, shaders written twice) where agents already fail most.
assumptions: Projects are usually one target, rarely both
Web app = real site with UI + 3D view
Assets, baked materials, humanoid skeletons travel as glTF; Godot import script keeps studio-owned materials
D can be added later
tripwires: Same game wanted on both targets 2+ times -> add portable level format (D)
Shader/physics duplication eats more time than assets save -> narrow to one target per year

history.change: User wants Godot for standalone games and three.js for web apps; options rewritten from single-engine choice to dual-target strategies.

decisions.title: How characters get their shape

options.A: Parametric character kits (template body + parts; skeleton/weights built once per template; import as reference)
options.B: Sculpt mode in the studio (SDF blends + brush)
options.D: Hand off to Blender via Blender MCP

decisions.caseAgainst: Kits can look samey; each new body type is days of template work; odd-shaped heroes hit kit limits. C-shapes + A-skeleton hybrid if variety matters more.
assumptions: Low-poly characters
Animation reliability > one-off variety
Standard humanoid bone names, T-pose
Import used as reference to fit kit params
Blender as escape hatch
tripwires: Users/you reject characters as samey after 10+ made -> add C-shaped parts or hybrid
Need a body type the kit can't cover 3+ times -> build template or use D

decisions.title: How studio materials become game textures

options.A: Auto-unwrap (xatlas) + GPU bake per asset, with density/padding/stretch checks
options.C: No bake: port procedural shaders to each engine
options.D: Unique bake for heroes, atlas for the rest

decisions.caseAgainst: Unique textures add up (memory on web/older hardware); auto-unwrap seams are least reliable on characters.
assumptions: Early projects are small
Bake reuses the studio's material shader, lighting-free
Kit characters use template seams
Atlas mode added when texture budget check fails
tripwires: A project's texture budget check fails -> add atlas mode (becomes D)

decisions.title: Where animation comes from
decisions.chosenTitle: Parametric motion in the studio (clips for one-off actions)

options.A: Clip library retargeted to kit skeleton + engine IK
options.B: Parametric motion ops in the studio (walk/run/idle from settings)

decisions.caseAgainst: Near toss-up with B: A breaks the 'every change is one reviewable setting' promise for motion. Tiebreaker: ship a playable character soon -> A; extend parametric philosophy to motion -> B.
assumptions: T-pose, standard humanoid names, <=4 weights, transforms applied
CC0/affordable clip library exists, licences checked
B planned as second step
All clips pass pose checks
tripwires: Asking for motion tweaks that clips can't express 3+ times -> start B
decisions.reasoning: User chose B over the lean A: extend the everything-is-a-setting idea to motion; library clips remain for attacks/emotes.

decisions.title: Game-ready checks and export profiles

options.A: Live game-profile checks every step + generated collision/LOD ops + engine round-trip on export

decisions.caseAgainst: Heavier, noisier steps; mid-build budget failures; export depends on headless Godot.
assumptions: Checks only for objects with a game profile
Budgets use pending state mid-build
Collision/LODs are generated ops
Khronos validator always runs
Godot installed on exporting machine
tripwires: Steps noticeably slower on big assets -> move heavy checks (round-trip) to export only

decisions.title: First game-shaped milestone

options.A: Walk around a tiny diorama (thin slice through all new parts, wk 5)

decisions.caseAgainst: Eight rough new parts at once make failures hard to localize; a rough kit template may teach wrong rigging lessons.
assumptions: ~full-time with Claude Code
In-flight materials/scenes/drag/import finished first
Each part ships tests + bench task 10-14
D is next milestone
tripwires: Character not walking in Godot by end of week 5 -> stop features, cut scope

decisions.title: How detailed faces get in cutscenes
decisions.chosenTitle: Stylized big-shape faces in the kit

options.A: Keep the low-poly face
options.B: Stylized big-shape faces in the kit (denser face region, ~15 speech + ~15 expression shapes generated)

decisions.caseAgainst: Stylized never equals realistic micro-detail; an acting face template is hard design and simple faces expose errors. C closer to realism for few heroes, accepting mismatch.
assumptions: Realistic mouth = natural speech, not photoreal
Low-poly stays
~30 shapes per character within file budget
Stylized face holds close-ups (verify in milestone)
tripwires: Close-up renders look lifeless after tuning -> denser face region or C for hero characters

decisions.title: How the face is rigged
decisions.chosenTitle: 15 speech shapes + ARKit-named subset + jaw/eye bones

options.A: 15 standard viseme shape keys + ARKit-named expression subset (~16) + jaw/eye/head bones

decisions.caseAgainst: Bets against future face capture: ARKit-52 input (iPhone, Azure) needs a lossy fold-down mapping; shape keys cost size and break on some Android GPUs.
assumptions: Lip sync mainly from audio/text (15 visemes)
Shapes generated from kit template
Face-shape budget check in game profiles
Fixed ARKit-52 → subset mapping if capture appears
tripwires: You start capturing performances on a phone -> extend to full ARKit 52

decisions.title: Where lip sync comes from
decisions.chosenTitle: Audio + script aligned locally, then smoothing

options.A: Any audio + script aligned locally (Rhubarb / Whisper + dictionary) → 15 shapes → smoothing (coarticulation, M/B/P closure, emotion)

decisions.caseAgainst: Alignment knows timing, not feeling: mouths can be flat without emotion layering; Audio2Face looks better if runnable; B fewer parts if all lines AI-voiced. All three feed one smoothing step.
assumptions: Dialogue pre-recorded/pre-generated
English first
Smoothing pass + closure checks are ours
D kept for drafting
tripwires: Mouths read flat after smoothing tuning -> try C via cloud on hero lines

decisions.title: Hands
decisions.chosenTitle: Full fingers, poses as settings, grip sockets on props

options.A: Full fingers (3 joints each), poses as settings (curl/spread/thumb), grip sockets on props, finger-through-prop check
options.D: Swappable hand shapes, no finger bones

decisions.caseAgainst: ~doubles bone count (25→55), hard knuckle weights, every touched prop needs a grip socket; B covers most acting in medium shots cheaply.
assumptions: Hands in close-up in cutscenes
Template designs knuckles once
Studio props get generated grip sockets
LODs/mobile may drop finger bones
tripwires: Web/mobile bone budget fails repeatedly -> drop finger bones in those profiles

decisions.title: Face, hands and body as one performance

options.A: One performance script per line (emotion, gaze, gestures, grip, posture) compiled to shared-beat channels + procedural life layer
options.B: Separate tracks lined up by hand
options.C: AI model generates whole-body motion from voice
options.D: Act it out on camera (MediaPipe) and retarget

decisions.caseAgainst: Rule-driven characters can feel tidy/repetitive; library gestures never invented; for key emotional scenes a real performance (D) wins — keep D as an override source.
assumptions: Dialogue-heavy, directed in words
Gesture library on decision-22 hand poses covers most acting
Seeded procedural life layer
Performance file is plain text, reviewable
tripwires: Characters read repetitive across 20+ lines -> add gesture variation + D overrides for key scenes
A commercially licensed gesture model for custom rigs appears -> add as a source

decisions.title: Where cutscenes are made and played
decisions.chosenTitle: Studio cutscene file + two thin players

options.A: Studio cutscene file (shots, cameras, cuts, lines+performances, audio, events) + generated Godot AnimationPlayer + small three.js player; storyboard review; dialogue branching in Yarn/JSON

decisions.caseAgainst: Inventing a format and two players; every new shot type lands in three places; Godot AnimationPlayer already does most — if Godot-only, B is less to build. Keep the format small with an escape hatch.
assumptions: Cutscenes in both targets
Small format + engine escape hatch
Storyboard frames for review
Branching in a dialogue tool
tripwires: Format grows past ~15 shot/event kinds -> stop and push extras to engine escape hatches

decisions.title: First cutscene milestone
decisions.chosenTitle: The Forge Lesson, talking-face checkpoint wk 4

options.A: 'The Forge Lesson' (2 characters, 4 shots, 3 lines) by wk 8, talking-face checkpoint wk 4, diorama wk 6

decisions.caseAgainst: Plan grows 6→8 weeks, diorama slips a week; week 3 kit is the most error-prone week; a failed checkpoint stalls everything. C keeps gameplay on schedule at the cost of kit rework.
assumptions: ~full-time with Claude Code
Test lines recorded or TTS voice by wk 4
Checkpoint and wk-8 tripwires
D is next
tripwires: Talking face doesn't read as speech after a week of tuning -> revisit 19-21
Cutscene not playing in Godot by wk 8 -> defer three.js player
